name: Structural identity TVT + Z - ANCC = const per well (ROGII Kaggle discussion; reused in 2nd, 4th, 8th, 10th, 14th, 22nd writeups and the Lukyanenko blog)
authors_org: Community finding from the Kaggle ROGII discussion board [uncertain: the original poster could not be identified; the page Kaggle search returns (discussion/701034, Nicolas Bridelance) only shows that the surface columns are in TVD/Z space, not TVT]. Stated independently by the 2nd place (AnchorCNN), 10th place (Can, solo), 8th place (Yuto part), 22nd place (Ochir's engine, U = TVT + Z), 14th place (keithtyser README) and Andrey Lukyanenko's blog. Verified locally in this study on all 773 training wells.
venue_link: Kaggle ROGII competition discussion + writeups: 2nd place (local C:/Users/Aadinarayan R/Desktop/CSE/projects/Erudition/2nd.txt, eq. 1 dTVT = dz_layer - dz); 10th place https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rogii-wellbore-geology-prediction/writeups/10th-place-solution-a-compass-not-a-map ; 8th place https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rogii-wellbore-geology-prediction/writeups/8th-place-pf-ranker ; 22nd place https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rogii-wellbore-geology-prediction/writeups/22nd-place-solution-five-engines-and-a-hard-less ; blog https://andlukyane.com/blog/rogii-geosteering-kaggle ; surface columns in TVD: https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/rogii-wellbore-geology-prediction/discussion/701034
code_availability: No dedicated code; the identity is a one-line data fact. Local verification script written for this study (scratchpad idcheck.py / seg.py / orc.py, not committed). In our repo the surface S = TVT + Z already appears in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_dataset.py (S_avg from the six formation columns, used by the Simulator's init_xy_local_fits for synthetic XY shifts) and in seq_NN_geo_prior.py (fold-safe IDW prior on S_rel = S - S0).
evidence_level: Verified directly on the local training data (773 wells, 3,783,989 suffix rows) in this study, plus consistent statements in 6+ competition writeups. Not peer-reviewed, but it is an exact property of how the host built the labels.
extreme_summary: TVT is exactly the expert-interpreted formation surface minus the wellbore Z plus a per-well constant: TVT + Z - ANCC is constant within every well to CSV rounding (per-well std 0.0066 ft, range 0.03-0.07 ft), and the six formation columns are parallel offsets of one surface (ANCC - BUDA std 0.003 ft). It is not a test-time constraint, because ANCC is absent from test files; it is a reparameterisation: predicting TVT = predicting the smooth surface A(MD) = TVT + Z, and all drift is error in the dip dA/dMD.
task_definition: Not a model. A data identity: for each training well, C_well = TVT(MD) + Z(MD) - ANCC(MD) is constant. Consequence: TVT(MD) = TVT_anchor + [A(MD) - A_anchor] - [Z(MD) - Z_anchor], so the only unknown in the blind zone is the change in the geological surface A along the path.
inputs: Train horizontal CSV columns: MD, X, Y, Z, ANCC, ASTNU, ASTNL, EGFDU, EGFDL, BUDA, TVT, GR, TVT_input. Test horizontal CSV columns: MD, X, Y, Z, GR, TVT_input only (verified on data/test/000d7d20__horizontal_well.csv). So ANCC and the other formation columns exist for training wells only (7 of 773 wells have ANCC entirely NaN; BUDA is complete for all 773). Our U-Net inputs (experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_cfg.py unet_static_channels) do not include any formation column; they include z_diff (row-to-row dZ in the suffix), tw_tvt_rel, seen_tvt_rel and tw_seen_tvt_abs_diff; the geo_* channels (geo_s_rel, geo_tvt_rel, geo_tvt_abs_diff, geo_dS, geo_tvt_diff, delta_geo_trend_rbf_5) are commented out in the baseline channel list.
target_parameterisation: Surface space u = A = TVT + Z (8th place U-Net synthetic generator, 22nd place Ochir beam-DP 'U = TVT + Z', 15th-silver style trackers) versus TVT space with dZ as input (2nd place: feed dz/dMD so the model only estimates the smooth dz_layer; our 1st-place reproduction: z_diff channel, TVT lattice). The 10th place author reports getting this backwards twice: build the state lattice on TVT (median suffix swing 26.4 ft, p95 54.4 ft) not on A (157.5 ft median swing, same as Z's 160.6 ft), but put the smoothness prior on dA/dMD (dip: p1/median/p99 = -0.065/+0.017/+0.072; std of dip change per 20 ft node 0.0096).
output_representation: Not applicable (identity). Implied options: per-column distribution over TVT (ours), or a piecewise-linear A(MD) with few breakpoints (expert interpretations are 'sequences of straight lines': 8th place measured median segment length about 98 ft and fault-like jumps at 3.1% of segments).
architecture: Not applicable. How top solutions exploited the identity: (1) 2nd place: dz/dMD input so the AnchorCNN learns only the structural slope; steps in dz_layer/dMD occur in about 10% of columns. (2) 4th place: LightGBM quantile regression predicts dA/dMD (A = ANCC) per 750 ft segment from X, Y, Z, azimuth and pitch, integrates it to a topography TVT prior plus a confidence band, and renders the band as the green image channel for a ConvNeXt V2 that predicts 8 control-point offsets. (3) 8th place: synthetic generator invents u_new = S_real (RDP piecewise-linear skeleton of a real surface) + d (piecewise-linear deviation field, AR(1) slope deviations rho about 0.248), then TVT_new = u_new - Z with the real trajectory; inventing TVT directly was detected by a real-vs-synthetic domain gate at AUC 1.0. (4) 10th place and Lukyanenko: kriged/IDW formation-top surfaces from training wells evaluated along the query path as a structural prior. (5) Our repo: Simulator.init_xy_local_fits fits dS = a dX + b dY on S_avg for synthetic XY shifts; seq_NN_geo_prior.py builds a fold-safe anisotropic IDW WLS prior on S.
core_mechanism: Drillers steer Z to follow the formation, so dTVT = dA - dZ with dZ known exactly for every row at test time. The high-frequency part of TVT is therefore free (it is -dZ), and all remaining uncertainty is the low-frequency geological surface A (dip plus occasional kinks/faults). Our own measurements on the 155-well holdout (0801_V2_ep150 predictions, pooled 4.978 ft) show the residual is dominated by low-order structure: removing a per-well constant gives 3.80 ft, a per-well line 3.08 ft, a heel-anchored slope only 3.51 ft, a per-well quadratic 2.46 ft; 58.6% of squared error lies more than 3,000 ft past the heel and 87% more than 1,500 ft past it. This is the same 'random-walk dip error' picture the 8th (6.44 -> 3.33 with per-well line oracle) and 10th (error correlation length 400-500 ft; 89% of SSE beyond 1,500 ft) places report.
training_objective: Not applicable. Possible uses: an auxiliary loss on dA/dMD (dip) or on the piecewise-linear structure of A (training labels available from TVT + Z for every training row, even for the 7 wells without ANCC), or a smoothness penalty on second differences of A along the decoded path.
decoding: Not applicable. Note for decoders: a per-column expectation over the TVT lattice is still Bayes-optimal for pooled RMSE; converting to A = TVT + Z changes nothing in the decode itself (Z is deterministic).
metric_consistent_decode: Neutral. The identity is a change of variables with a known deterministic offset (Z), so RMSE on TVT equals RMSE on A; any mean decode in either space is equally RMSE-optimal.
evidence_scope: Per well (the constant C_well is per well); cross-well use requires spatial interpolation of A (kriging/IDW/tabular dip models), which several teams found transfers poorly to the hidden set.
prefix_conditioning: The identity lets the known prefix fix C_well and A_anchor exactly (TVT_input + Z at the last known row), which our dataset already does (s0 = TVT_input[last_seen] + Z[last_seen] in seq_NN_dataset.py; tw_tvt_rel / seen_tvt_rel are relative to that anchor). The prefix also gives the recent dip dA/dMD; extrapolating it is weak (our check: last-200-row prefix slope extrapolation of A = 43.4 ft pooled over all 773 training suffixes vs 107.5 ft for holding A constant; 10th place: 12.60 vs 15.91 flat).
propose_vs_select: Not applicable; can feed a proposal (structural prior channel / candidate) or a constraint.
physical_constraints: Exact: TVT + Z - ANCC = C_well (std 0.0066 ft); all six formation surfaces are parallel (ANCC - BUDA std 0.003 ft within a well). Approximate: A(MD) is piecewise linear with sparse kinks and rare jumps (2nd place: steps in about 10% of columns; 8th place: median segment about 98 ft, jumps 3.1%). [uncertain] My own rough kink count (about 10 slope changes per 1,000 ft using a 10-row smoothed slope and a 0.004 threshold) is sensitive to the 0.01 ft rounding and should not be relied on.
dataset: ROGII Kaggle training set: 773 horizontal wells with paired typewells, 3,783,989 scored suffix rows, MD step 1 ft (median). Test/hidden files lack the formation columns.
synthetic_to_real: Directly relevant: synthetic TVT paths should be generated in surface space (A = piecewise-linear skeleton + deviation, TVT = A - Z) to keep dTVT ~ -dZ coupling realistic (8th place: direct TVT invention was trivially separable, AUC 1.0). Our Simulator already works in S space for its XY-shift augmentation (init_xy_local_fits on S_avg), and 85% of our training wells are synthetic. [uncertain] Whether every synthetic path mode in our Simulator preserves the dTVT = dA - dZ coupling with a piecewise-linear A was not audited line by line.
metric_and_performance: Identity accuracy (this study, local data): per-well std of TVT + Z - ANCC mean 0.00657 ft (max 0.0087), per-well range 0.03-0.07 ft (matches the discussion's '~0.03 ft' and the 10th place '0.07 ft = CSV rounding'); identical for ASTNU and BUDA. Oracles on our holdout (0801_V2_ep150, pooled 4.978 ft): per-well constant removed 3.80, per-well line removed 3.08, heel-anchored slope removed 3.51, per-well quadratic removed 2.46. External oracles: 10th place on A with piecewise-linear fits: one anchored line 7.59, one free line 5.96, two segments 2.43, three segments 1.44 (relative to their chain). Uses: 4th place topography-only prior private 12.6 (weak) -> 10.8 with a stronger TabPFN/RealMLP/LightGBM dip ensemble; 6th place GR-free physical dip prior alone CV 10.1 / private 9.34, but injected into PF likelihood CV 6.98 -> 6.50 and aligned CV with LB.
comparability: Oracle numbers on our holdout are directly comparable (same 155 wells, same pooled RMSE). External numbers are 5-fold CV or LB on other models; use them only for direction.
validation_protocol: The identity itself needs no validation. Anything built from other wells' A (kriging, IDW, dip regression) must be strictly fold-safe (6th place: leak in the dip field inflates CV and collapses on private), and must be priced under realistic donor density: 10th place found the hidden wells are more isolated (median distance to nearest training well 683 ft vs 470 ft among training wells); a neighbour-surface stage gained 0.18 CV but lost 0.33 public (2.95 sigma) [though it would have scored 6.179 vs 6.269 private, so the evidence is mixed].
inference_budget: Negligible for the identity; a tabular dip model or IDW prior is CPU-cheap (our geo prior takes about 10 s for 155 wells after caching).
repeated_layers: No direct help: the identity does not tell which repeated GR band the bit is in. It helps indirectly by constraining how fast A can change (dip bounds), which narrows the set of plausible band jumps; a jump to a band 15 ft away within a short MD span would need an implausible dip or a fault.
drift: This is the main target. Drift = integrated error in dip dA/dMD. Levers: (a) a better dip prior from geometry (4th place tabular dA/dMD with quantile band; 6th place fold-safe dip field), (b) a piecewise-linear structural prior on A, (c) synthetic training in A space so the network learns realistic dip statistics. Caveat from the 10th place: their final model already beat the best single straight line, so below about 5 ft on their scale gains must come from fitting bends, not a single drift slope; our ConvNeXt (4.98) is at 3.08 after removing a per-well line, so a single-line correction could at most gain about 1.9 ft if it were perfectly predictable, but 10th and 22nd place found drift direction essentially unpredictable from observables (OOF drift correctors: CV -0.25, LB +0.34).
uncertainty_and_calibration: The 4th place produced calibrated confidence intervals for dA/dMD (Pearson corr between predicted sigma and actual error 0.31 -> 0.40 with the stronger ensemble) and rendered them as an image channel, letting the vision model learn when to trust topography. Our geo prior exposes geo_nbr_std, geo_nbr_dS_std and geo_radial_extrap_score diagnostics that serve the same purpose but are not in the baseline channel list.
where_to_use: (1) Input channel: a structural-prior probability channel in the cost image (P(TVT > level | dip prior)), like the 4th place green channel, built from a fold-safe dip model with an uncertainty band; our geo_* channels are the closest existing code. (2) Auxiliary target: predict dA/dMD per column as a second head (label = d(TVT + Z)/dMD, available for every training row). (3) Synthetic generator audit: make sure synthetic TVT = A_synthetic - Z with A piecewise linear. (4) Diagnostics: report errors in A-slope space to separate drift from band confusion.
error_mode_targeted: Drift (~25% of squared error), secondarily broad humps; not band confusion.
gap_vs_our_implementation: What we already do: (a) z_diff is an input channel, so the network sees dZ and can learn dTVT = dA - dZ (the 2nd-place insight); (b) the anchor fixes C_well via s0 = TVT_input + Z at the last known row; (c) the Simulator uses S_avg (mean of the six formation columns, i.e. TVT + Z + const) for XY-shift synthetic augmentation; (d) seq_NN_geo_prior.py builds a fold-safe anisotropic IDW WLS prior on S with neighbour diagnostics. What we do not do: (1) no geo/structural channel in the baseline U-Net input (geo_* channels commented out; the XY geo-prior was tried only as a post-hoc hump picker, which failed); (2) no uncertainty-banded structural prior channel (4th place style) and no tabular dip model from X, Y, Z, azimuth, inclination; (3) no auxiliary dip (dA/dMD) head or smoothness loss on A; (4) no explicit check that synthetic paths follow piecewise-linear A. The identity cannot be used as a hard test-time constraint: ANCC is absent from test, so TVT + Z - ANCC = const adds no information beyond what z_diff and the anchor already give.
proposed_experiment: E1 (zero training, diagnostic): extend posterior_analysis.py (or a new script next to posterior_geo_pick.py) to decompose holdout error into A-space components per well: residual after removing constant, line, quadratic, and after a 2-3 segment piecewise-linear fit; attribute each well's error to drift vs band confusion using the existing wrong_mode/blend labels. Control: current 60-epoch and ep150 predictions. E2 (input channel): re-enable a subset of the existing geo channels in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_cfg.py unet_static_channels, specifically geo_tvt_abs_diff (|level - prior TVT|) plus a new 'geo_prior_cdf' channel = Phi((level - prior_TVT)/sigma_prior) where sigma_prior comes from geo_nbr_dS_std scaled by distance past the heel; keep everything else fixed; train 60 epochs and compare with the 60-epoch baseline (5.47) on the 155 holdout wells with paired bootstrap; then 150 epochs if it passes the +-0.39 noise floor. Also run it with the prior computed under 'realistic donor density' (drop training wells within ~500 ft of each holdout well) to price the 10th-place isolation effect. E3 (tabular dip prior, 4th-place style): fit LightGBM quantile models (q10/q50/q90) for dA/dMD per 250-750 ft segment from segment-midpoint X, Y, Z, azimuth, inclination, fold-safe over the 618 training wells; integrate to a TVT prior band and use it as the E2 channel instead of IDW. E4 (auxiliary head): add a per-column regression head for dA/dMD (label d(TVT+Z)/dMD smoothed over 16-32 ft) with weight 0.1 in seq_NN_train.py; compare with baseline at 60 epochs. E5 (synthetic audit): in seq_NN_dataset.py Simulator, verify that synthetic TVT paths satisfy TVT = A - Z with A piecewise linear; if not, add an 8th-place style generator mode (RDP skeleton of a real A + AR(1) slope deviation + decoy +-15 ft) and compare.
implementation_effort: E1 low (analysis script). E2 low-medium (channels already implemented; add one CDF channel and retrain). E3 medium (new tabular model + fold-safe integration). E4 low-medium (one extra head + loss). E5 medium.
gpu_cost: [uncertain] E1/E3 CPU only. E2/E4: one 60-epoch ConvNeXt-small run each on the RTX 5060 8 GB (same cost as existing 60-epoch ablations), plus a 150-epoch confirmation run if promising. Extra channels add negligible compute.
distillation_compatibility: Good. Extra input channels or an auxiliary head carry over to the FastViT student unchanged (the student gets the same input tensor; KD on output posteriors is unaffected).
error_correlation_with_ours: A structural-prior channel changes what the same network sees, so diversity is modest; a standalone tabular dip prior has very different errors (weak alone: 4th place 12.6/10.8, 6th place CV 10.1) and is most useful as an input or likelihood term, not as a blend member.
risk: (1) Our XY geo-prior already failed as a post-hoc hump picker, and 10th and 4th place both observed that neighbour/topography information improves CV but can hurt the hidden set because hidden wells are more isolated and the model over-trusts topography (4th place deliberately kept a weaker topography model). (2) Drift direction appeared unpredictable in 10th and 22nd place studies (drift correctors CV -0.25 / LB +0.34; per-well blend weights no better than a scalar). (3) The identity itself is not a new constraint at test time; expectations of 'removing drift' from it are overstated. (4) Gains may fall under the +-0.39 ft single-run noise floor, requiring paired bootstrap or multiple seeds. (5) Auxiliary dip loss could conflict with the per-column CE if weighted too high.
notes: Local verification details: 773 training wells; ANCC NaN in 7 wells (0.9% of rows); per-well std of TVT + Z - ANCC mean 0.00657 ft (range 0.0057-0.0087), per-well max-min 0.03-0.07 ft; identical behaviour for ASTNU and BUDA; ANCC - BUDA constant within a well (std mean 0.0027 ft), i.e. the six columns are one surface plus constants, so the formation columns carry one degree of freedom per row. Surface columns are in negative TVD units like Z (discussion 701034). The 22nd place also found a second exact per-well invariant from the host's GR normalization: beta = <GR_lateral, TW_GR(TVT_true)> / <GR, GR> = 0.99904 +- 0.001, which pins a scalar of the hidden path but has a multimodal root set (median 8 solutions within +-40 ft); worth a separate look as a test-legal constraint. Holdout gain check (this study): a heel-anchored global gain on (pred - TVT_anchor) is 0.98 in-sample (4.978 -> 4.971) and 0.96 cross-fitted (5.011 +- 0.064, worse), so the 6th/10th place 'de-shrink' gains (a ~1.02-1.03) do not transfer to our ConvNeXt, which is not amplitude-shrunk.
